turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, doctor. I've brought my brother, Mr Dlamini, through from the waiting room. Sorry if I seem half asleep, my little one was coughing the whole night.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Morning. Uh, have a seat, sir. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I have come about a lump in the groin, the right side. It appears when I lift at work.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): A lump with lifting. How long have you noticed it?
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Three months, doctor. After a heavy shift he stands there holding the right side. I've seen it.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Forgive me, sister, that is not accurate. It has been six weeks, not three months. I do not wish to give you the wrong history, doctor.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mhm. You say six weeks, she says three months, so I'll put it down as roughly six weeks to three months. We won't settle it finer today. Tell me how the lump behaves.

[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): If I lift a bag of cement, or push the wheelbarrow, the lump comes out. When I lie down on the bed it goes away completely. By the evening there is a mild ache, nothing severe.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): And he is up at night with it. I hear him in the passage, he can't sleep.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): With respect, that is not the case. I sleep perfectly well. The ache is only in the evening, and it is mild. It does not wake me.

[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so it comes out with strain and slips back when you lie flat. Err, what I think is going on is a bit of bowel, or some fatty tissue, pushing through a weak spot in the groin muscle. The pressure of lifting forces it out, and lying down lets it drop back. That picture is an inguinal hernia, though I can't completely rule out a lymph node.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not vomited.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nausea? Any change in the bowels? Pain in the tummy itself, apart from the groin?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No nausea, doctor. The bowels are regular, as usual. There is no pain in the tummy, only the groin.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And passing urine, any burning, or trouble getting it going?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. That side of things is quite normal.

[SEG0018] person_1 (NURSE): Vitals while I remember. Blood pressure one nineteen over seventy-seven, ag no, wrong line, it's one oh nine over seventy-seven, pulse seventy-six, temperature thirty-six point four. Last time in March the pressure was one-forty over eighty-eight.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Those are comfortable numbers. Any allergy to medicines, Mr Dlamini?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): None, doctor. I have never reacted to a medicine.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what medicines are you actually taking?

[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Only Panado, two tablets at night, which is one gram, for the ache. I have used it for about two weeks. I did take broofen, four hundred milligrams, for the same ache, but I stopped that three weeks ago because it upset my stomach.
[SEG0023] person_1 (NURSE): There were Grandpa powders in his bag as well. I saw the box this morning.
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): That box belongs to a colleague on the site, doctor. I have never taken Grandpa powders myself.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we ignore the Grandpa. Any operations in the past? Diabetes, heart problems, anything ongoing?

[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No operations at all. No diabetes and no heart trouble, I am otherwise well. About two years ago the day hospital did a scan of the groin and they said the result was borderline. They did not call it a hernia at that time.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Borderline scan, and we haven't got the report in front of us, so I'll just note what you were told. Do you smoke?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): I have never smoked, doctor. I do take a beer on a Saturday after work, only the one.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the work itself is heavy, from what you've said.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. I am a manual labourer on a building site in Germiston. Cement, scaffolding, wheelbarrows. I stay in the back room at my sister's house.

[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): Ja, he's with me. I leave for my clinic shift before he does, so I don't always see how he is in the morning. My own back has been sore from the extra shifts, but that's me, not him.

[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me examine you. Lie flat and cough for me. There is a soft swelling in the right groin, it bulges when you cough, and it reduces when I press it back. Nothing on the left, and the abdomen is soft and not tender.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): It is slightly sore when you press on the lump, doctor, if I may mention it. Not severely.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, I agree, mildly tender right over the swelling, and nowhere else. Well, I'm happy to call this a reducible right inguinal hernia. The lymph node is much less likely, now that it reduces so easily.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I don't think another scan will change the plan today. I'll refer you to the surgeons at the provincial hospital, and they'll send a clinic date. Until then, no heavy lifting. No cement bags, no wheelbarrows, no scaffolding.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the lump gets stuck out and you cannot push it back, or if you start vomiting, or the pain turns severe, go straight to casualty. Don't wait for the clinic.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand, doctor. I will ask the foreman for lighter duties. Is an operation certain?

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): The surgeons will almost certainly discuss a repair, but that decision is theirs, not mine this morning. No new tablets from me. Carry on with the Panado at night if the ache is there, one gram, and don't go above that.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): May I still walk to work, doctor? It is about twenty minutes. I do not want to do harm.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Walking is fine. It is straining and heavy lifting I want stopped. If the ache builds on the walk, slow down, but ordinary walking should be alright. I won't book you back here routinely, the surgical clinic takes it from here.

[SEG0041] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take the referral letter to reception on the way out, they'll book the surgical clinic. And doctor, just so the file is straight, the March reading stays the old one. Today's pressure is the one oh nine over seventy-seven.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I am grateful for your time, and for the clear advice. I will be careful with the lifting.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Look after yourself, Mr Dlamini. Sister will sort the letter.
[SEG0044] person_1 (NURSE): Come, we'll get it stamped. You'll be alright.

spec.situation: Manual worker with a groin lump that appears on lifting and goes away lying down; mild ache by evening; no vomiting; surgical referral planned, advice on lifting.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Patient explicitly denies sleep disturbance and says it does not wake him.
bad.text: Difficulty sleeping (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=nurse, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: Broofen 400 mg for ache and discontinued are supported; stop timing three weeks ago is omitted.
bad.text: broofen (generic_name=ibuprofen, dose=400 mg, indication=groin ache, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Past groin scan with borderline recalled result is supported; requested_by patient is not stated.
bad.text: Groin scan (type=imaging, status=completed, requested_by=patient, indication=Groin lump, result recalled as borderline)

omissions.text: The recorded sleep symptom is wrong: the patient explicitly denied sleep disturbance, saying he sleeps perfectly well and the mild evening ache does not wake him.
Ibuprofen/Broofen was stopped 3 weeks ago because it upset his stomach.
The patient denied ever taking Grandpa powders; the box seen belonged to a colleague.
Past blood pressure from March was mentioned as 140/88 mmHg, distinct from today's 109/77.
The prior groin scan was done about 2 years ago at the day hospital, and they did not call it a hernia at that time.
No new tablets were prescribed at this visit.
The doctor said he would not book routine follow-up here because the surgical clinic would take over.
The patient planned to ask his foreman for lighter duties.
